zebralogic.title: PreserveExactCase
zebralogic.principle: Copy every attribute value exactly as it appears in the puzzle, preserving case, spacing, and punctuation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever an attribute value is mentioned in a clue or placed in the final grid.
zebralogic.example: Outputting "OnePlus 9" instead of the required "oneplus 9" causes a mismatch with the reference solution.

zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: Interpret clues stating "X is directly left of Y" as X's house number = Y's house number − 1 (and similarly for "directly right of").
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrase "directly left of" or "directly right of".
zebralogic.example: Treating "directly left of" as any leftward position, allowing gaps between the houses.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: Treat clues that say "X is somewhere to the left of Y" as a strict ordering constraint X < Y (and similarly for "right of").
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses "somewhere to the left/right of" without specifying distance.
zebralogic.example: Assuming X must be adjacent to Y when the clue only requires X to be somewhere left of Y.

zebralogic.title: AdjacencyWithoutOrientation
zebralogic.principle: Interpret clues that state "X and Y are next to each other" as |X − Y| = 1, with no implied left/right orientation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says two entities are "next to each other" or "adjacent" without direction.
zebralogic.example: Assuming X is left of Y when the clue only says they are adjacent, thereby fixing an orientation that is not given.

zebralogic.title: ExactDistance
zebralogic.principle: For clues stating "There are N houses between X and Y", enforce |X − Y| = N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific number of houses separating two entities.
zebralogic.example: Using |X‑Y| = N instead of N + 1, which places the houses one position too close.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that two attributes refer to the same entity, treat them as a combined attribute (link them).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue equates two different categories (e.g., "the person who loves soccer is Carol").
zebralogic.example: Treating "soccer" and "Carol" as unrelated instead of linking the sport to the name, leading to contradictory assignments.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number, assign that attribute to that house immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions an explicit house number (e.g., "the person who uses a OnePlus 9 is in the second house").
zebralogic.example: Ignoring the explicit house number and treating it as a relative clue, which can place the attribute in the wrong house.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Ensure the final JSON output is syntactically valid: all arrays and objects are properly closed, keys are quoted, and commas are placed correctly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Before submitting the answer, check the JSON for any syntax errors.
zebralogic.example: Missing a closing bracket in the JSON, causing the verifier to reject the answer.

zebralogic.title: ChildAttributeLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue mentions a child's name (e.g., "the person whose child is named X"), treat X as the value of the Child attribute and link it to the corresponding parent.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: In puzzles that include a separate child‑name category.
zebralogic.example: Confusing the child's name with the parent's name and linking the wrong attributes, leading to an invalid parent‑child pairing.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: Output the solution JSON as the very last part of the response and keep any preceding reasoning concise, ensuring the answer fits within the token limit and is not truncated.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After completing reasoning, emit only the final JSON and stop generation immediately.
zebralogic.example: Including long explanatory text after the JSON, causing the JSON to be cut off or omitted, which leads to an incomplete answer being rejected.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats attribute strings as case‑insensitive and rewrites them, losing the exact spelling required by the verifier.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy each attribute value verbatim from the puzzle statement, preserving case, spacing, and punctuation.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: A clue is overlooked or misinterpreted, so the resulting assignment violates the puzzle's logic.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Systematically translate every clue into a concrete constraint before solving, and verify that all constraints are satisfied by the final grid.

zebralogic.description: Malformed JSON due to missing closing brackets
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model stops generation early or loses track of nesting, producing an incomplete JSON structure.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After constructing the JSON, double‑check that every opening bracket/brace has a matching closing one before finalising the answer.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The child name is treated as a regular attribute or is confused with the parent's name, breaking the parent‑child equivalence clues.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Treat child names as a distinct attribute category and enforce the explicit parent‑child equivalence clues before solving other constraints.

zebralogic.description: Generation truncation due to token limit
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model generates too much text (e.g., lengthy reasoning after the solution), exceeding the allowed token budget and cutting off the JSON or the entire answer.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise, place the final JSON at the very end of the response, and stop generation immediately after the JSON so the output stays within the token budget.
